description: A synthetic orbital-operations console for reviewing conjunction alerts and testing a one-impulse correction. Operators select one of three close-pass incidents, inspect a geocentric track, scrub or play the forecast, adjust radial/prograde delta-v, and compare the result with the zero-burn reference. A bounded grid sweep can suggest a low-magnitude clearance candidate.

numericalAssumptions: Two-dimensional inertial orbital plane around a fixed spherical Earth; μ = 398600.4418 km³/s² and Earth reference radius = 6371 km.

Each craft is propagated independently as a point mass under central inverse-square gravity using classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta with a default 20 s step. The 20 s map is piecewise linear between samples for closest-approach estimation.

A plotted maneuver is an instantaneous delta-v at epoch, resolved along local radial and prograde-tangential unit vectors. The interface's bounded candidate sweep checks radial/tangential components from −2 to +2 m/s in 0.2 m/s increments; it reports the lowest-magnitude grid candidate meeting 5 km when one is found, otherwise the best miss in that grid.
The 5 km response ring and 1 km critical band are UI triage thresholds only; they are not collision probabilities, object-size criteria, covariance bounds, or certified maneuver recommendations.

Incident states are synthetic. Each debris state is seeded by defining a small relative offset and velocity at a future encounter epoch, then numerically integrating backward in the same two-body model. No live catalog or celestial data is used.
The map uses one linear radial kilometer scale for Earth and orbital shells. The forecast horizon is user-selectable from 1 to 6 hours.
limitations: No atmospheric drag, Earth oblateness/J2, third-body perturbations, mutual gravity, finite-duration thrust, attitude, object dimensions, fragmentation model, tracking uncertainty, or conjunction probability.
The planar model has no inclination or cross-track motion; the displayed two-dimensional miss distance can therefore differ materially from a full three-dimensional encounter.
Closest approach is interpolated along each 20 s relative-position segment; no root-finding refinement of the nonlinear continuous trajectory is performed.
